key_insight: Pretrained large-scale video generation models implicitly encode rich 3D spatial priors that can be extracted and reused to give models fine-grained geometric reasoning without relying on explicit 3D data.
problem_solved: Multimodal models are spatially blind — they struggle with detailed geometry and physical dynamics — and existing solutions rely on scarce explicit 3D data or complex geometric scaffolds that limit generalization.
method: Probe and extract spatio-temporal latents from pretrained video generation models that contain implicit 3D structure.
Distill those implicit priors into compact geometric prediction heads (e.g., depth, normals, occupancy, dynamics) with minimal or no explicit 3D supervision.
Align generation-derived priors to downstream scene-understanding tasks via lightweight adapters and task-specific finetuning for improved generalization.
impact: Enables robust 3D-aware scene understanding without expensive 3D datasets or heavy geometric engineering, accelerating deployment of spatially competent multimodal systems in robotics, AR/VR, and vision-language applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained video generator -> latent extraction -> distillation -> geometric prediction heads (depth/occupancy/dynamics).
Before/after examples: scenes where baseline MLLM fails spatial reasoning vs. model using implicit 3D priors succeeding.
Latent-space visualization (e.g., t-SNE) showing clustering by 3D structure or viewpoint.
Performance chart: task accuracy or error vs. methods that use explicit 3D supervision, showing comparable or superior results with less 3D data.
paper_title: Generation Models Know Space: Unleashing Implicit 3D Priors for Scene Understanding
paper_authors: Xianjin Wu, Dingkang Liang, Tianrui Feng, Kui Xia, Yumeng Zhang
